pr_title: Fix JSON perf regressions reported by #73242.
pr_body:
I was able to isolate the perf regression to using object initializer syntax in the state structs introduced in #72789. Not sure why, @EgorBo any insights?

Fix #73242.

> Also WriteJson

Performance regressions in polymorphic serialization are expected and intentional, see https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/72789#issuecomment-1198437536. We should close that one. I'm not sure what might have impacted deserialization, will investigate.

review_comments:
Alternative workaround:
```csharp
ReadStack readStack = default;
readStack.SupportContinuation = true
```

I'm just reverting to what we had previously here.

I'm still curious though, would have expected that `ReadStack readStack = new ReadStack();` is equivalent to `ReadStack readStack = default;` when it comes to structs.

it is. The problem is in the object initialization syntax - Roslyn creates a struct copy, see 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/523221/182668518-b83ff4ab-b6b5-4639-ae33-cf84b68f44d7.png)

and since the struct is quite huge such a copy is expensive.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/523221/182669120-53d4beb9-d454-449c-8a59-039af623cb2f.png)
UPD: it's not memset, but memcpy
Interesting, thanks. Would have assumed that it simply decompiles to what `Good` is doing.

> It's tracked by https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/8887

Maybe change Roslyn's behaviour instead?

> > It's tracked by #8887
> 
> Maybe change Roslyn's behaviour instead?

no, it's a correct IL and such patterns might appear in other places or/and after inlining
